scope: Fixture runs establish mechanics, not a measured benefit. Deterministic fixture providers decide every call, manual-clock times are declared, and the failures are planted where each policy acts, so the differences between arms follow from the fixtures and the policy under test. Scheduler overhead is real local time on one machine. No policy becomes a default, and no number here is a product, README or roadmap claim.

reasons: fixture providers and planted failures establish mechanics, not a measured benefit
no held-out quality, cost or latency criteria are decided for any policy
live evaluation needs an approved budget and decided thresholds

protocol.one_change: each case's baseline and policy arms come from one configuration and differ only in the varied policy; differs_in lists the keys on which they differ
protocol.attempts: every call or attempt is recorded, failed, cancelled, refused and rejected ones included
protocol.correlated_errors: failures one node caused (a cancelled or unknown sibling) form one group; other failures that share an outcome, error type, failure class and message form one group

executors.reference: a minimal asyncio executor: each ready node's provider call, with no checkpoint, budget, trace or acceptance

scheduler_overhead.transport: OpenAIResponsesProvider on the shared fake Responses transport (tests/fakes.py), replies scripted per step
scheduler_overhead.latency: each wire call, a generation or an input-token count, waits the declared latency first
scheduler_overhead.order: the executors rotate their order with each repetition
scheduler_overhead.overhead: each executor's elapsed time minus the reference's in the same repetition, per run and per node; store_ms is the time spent in checkpoint and journal store methods, reported apart and subtracted only in median_overhead_excluding_store_ms; extra_wire_latency_ms is the declared latency of the wire calls an executor makes beyond the reference's (the durable runtime's input-token counts), which every overhead figure includes
scheduler_overhead.note: Real monotonic time on one machine: machine-specific, never a product claim.
